title: Mandatory fuel price reporting (Queensland)
summary: Queensland required fuel retailers to report prices for publication from midday on 3 December 2018, initially as a two-year trial.

instruments.title: Fair Trading (Fuel Price Reporting) Regulation 2018
instruments.provisions: Parts 1 (other than ss 1-2), 2 and 3 from 3 December 2018 at midday

direction_rationale: Real-time public price data lower motorists' search costs, which should narrow retail margins, but they also let rival retailers see each other's prices at once, which can make tacit coordination and price cycles easier to sustain.
comparison: Staggered adoption 2016-2025. WA (FuelWatch, reporting since 2001) is always treated; the ACT has no mandatory scheme (a voluntary FuelCheck pilot from November 2022, not checked); states not yet reporting at each date.
confounders: crude oil and terminal gate price movements
temporary halving of fuel excise (30 Mar to 28 Sep 2022)
notes: Began as a two-year trial; the gap scan reports it now runs to 1 September 2029 (not checked).

verified.notes: Read on the Queensland register (legislative history): notified 16 November 2018; Parts 1-3 commenced 3 December 2018 at midday.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Retailers must report every price change for publication, so motorists can find the cheapest fuel. Lower search costs should sharpen price competition, but rivals also see each other's prices at once, which can help them coordinate.

marks.reason: Real-time public prices cut motorists' search costs; the risk that rivals use them to coordinate tempers the gain.
Retailers must register sites and report each price change within a set time.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation found no detectable effect on fuel prices (grade Weak).
